digest.component_or_area: LLM prompt caching and cache breakpoint placement in plan-review passes
propositions: Cache breakpoints sit at the END of pass-specific stance suffixes rather than at the shared-prefix boundary, causing within-run verifier passes to write new cache instead of reading the finder's write, wasting premium-rate tokens.

Single-step plan-review passes (all five passes in leaf-review shape) write cache on every call at premium rates but never read within the run, because each pass's breakpoint differs after its stance suffix, creating unique cache keys despite byte-identical leading content.

Cross-ticket prefix variation is BY DESIGN (the plan is embedded in the marked prefix for within-run fan-out reuse) and not a defect; the real prize is placing a second breakpoint at the shared-prefix boundary so same-ticket re-reviews within TTL and within-run pass-to-pass reuse both hit.

The diagnostic warn_if_cache_ineffective only flags write==0 AND read==0, missing the write-every-call-never-read shape on plan-bearing passes; this class of inefficiency is invisible to telemetry and costs ~9.2-9.5k cache-write tokens per leaf review with zero benefit.

The prerequisite-verifier template places the plan at line 16 after its stance, breaking byte-identity with other plan-bearing passes' leading bytes and preventing cross-pass reads even if breakpoints aligned.
